answer: Require each identity to complete a sequential verifiable-delay puzzle before it can trade, a computation that cannot be sped up by running many copies in parallel. Like a dune that only shifts grain by grain, the delay is fixed in wall-clock time, so one operator spawning a plume of fake accounts must wait the full delay for each, in turn. Standing attaches to the puzzle's vertex, a single public key whose chain of completed delays proves continuous, costly presence. An attacker therefore pays time, not just copies, per Sybil, while honest agents pay the delay once.
